items.title: Levin topographic map sheet, 1973
items.credit: Land Information New Zealand (LINZ), via Mapspast and Wikimedia Commons.
items.altText: A 1973 topographic map of Levin, showing the town and two railway stations.
items.caption: A 1:63,360 NZMS 1 sheet for Levin, printed in 1973.
items.context: This is a contemporary example of New Zealand paper topographic mapping. It is not an NZLRI worksheet and does not show the inventory land units described in this chapter.

items.title: Intergraph CLIX workstation, late 1980s
items.credit: Gigs, Wikimedia Commons contributor; released into the public domain.
items.altText: An Intergraph CLIX workstation with a monitor, keyboard and console.
items.caption: An Intergraph CLIX workstation from the late 1980s, photographed when it was decommissioned in the late 1990s.
items.context: The photographer identifies this as a late-1980s workstation and says it was photographed during decommissioning in the late 1990s. Its location and use are not identified, so it is included as representative period equipment and not as a New Zealand GIS installation.

items.title: Gisborne–East Coast land use capability map, 1967
items.licence: Free to use and redistribute with acknowledgement: Sourced from LINZ. Crown Copyright reserved.
items.credit: New Zealand Department of Lands and Survey; source original from LINZ; digitised by the National Library of New Zealand. Acknowledgement: Sourced from LINZ. Crown Copyright reserved.
items.altText: A coloured 1967 land use capability survey map for the Gisborne–East Coast region, with mapped classes and land-resource information.
items.caption: Land use capability survey, Gisborne–East Coast Region, 1967. Sourced from LINZ. Crown Copyright reserved.
items.context: The National Library catalogue describes this first-edition regional survey as a 1967 map at 1:126,720, with sheets for land capability, recommended land use and rock-type erodibility. It is an example of the paper classification and mapping work that preceded digital inventory use.

items.title: Te Kuiti Land Development Office, 1974–1984
items.credit: Archives New Zealand; photograph by an unidentified photographer; via Wikimedia Commons.
items.altText: The Te Kuiti Land Development Office building used by the Lands and Survey Department during 1974–1984.
items.caption: The Te Kuiti Land Development Office building, used by the Lands and Survey Department during 1974–1984. Photograph date not recorded.
items.context: The Archives New Zealand description identifies this as the building occupied by the Te Kuiti Land Development Office during 1974–1984; the photograph date is not specified. It shows a provincial land-administration office, not the national cadastral database team or a GIS workplace.

items.title: New Zealand District Health Board boundaries, 2001–2010
items.commonsTitle: File:New Zealand District Health Board Map 2001–10 (Blank).svg
items.credit: Stats NZ; compiled and edited by Air55; based in part on 2006 District Health Board data from the Ministry of Health; via Wikimedia Commons.
items.altText: An outline map of New Zealand divided into District Health Board boundaries.
items.caption: District Health Board boundaries in force from 2001 until the Otago–Southland merger in 2010.
items.context: This map shows later District Health Board geography, not the census-area denominator used in the 1990s public-health analysis discussed here. It is included to show the administrative health regions that followed.

items.title: Ministry of Works field trip, Gisborne, 1971
items.commonsTitle: File:Government Buildings, Lowe Street with M. O. W. Staff preparing a field trip with a Land Rover, Gisborne, (28445301672).jpg
items.credit: W. Neill; Archives New Zealand, reference R24802259 / AAQT 6539 W3537 113 / A97130; via Wikimedia Commons.
items.altText: Ministry of Works staff prepare for a field trip beside a Land Rover in Gisborne.
items.caption: Ministry of Works staff prepare a field trip in Gisborne, March 1971.
items.context: This Archives New Zealand photograph shows Ministry of Works staff preparing a Gisborne field trip in March 1971. It illustrates a government fieldwork setting before mobile GIS; it is not evidence of a GIS-based field workflow.

items.title: Victoria Square aerial image, Christchurch, 1975
items.credit: Land Information New Zealand, New Zealand Aerial Mapping, New Zealand Aerial Surveys and the Royal New Zealand Air Force; via Wikimedia Commons.
items.altText: An aerial image of Victoria Square in Christchurch, circa 1975.
items.caption: Victoria Square, Christchurch, in an aerial image from 1975.
items.context: This 1975 aerial image predates the Te Maari eruption and was not part of the 2012 UAV survey described here. It provides an earlier aerial-imaging comparison; it does not depict the Tongariro survey site.
